items.title: On 'tense' Antonelli's big weekend, this was Hamilton's day
items.summary: As Kimi Antonelli bids to become F1's youngest world champion, veteran Lewis Hamilton rolled back the years to take his first Ferrari pole.

items.title: Verstappen clears the air with Lawson, but keeps opinion on Racing Bulls F1 seat to himself
items.summary:
Max Verstappen qualified fourth for the Formula 1 Mexico City Grand Prix, but will have to drop one place on the starting grid, meaning he will start from the third row. The reason is remarkable, to say the least: contact with Liam Lawson - two drivers from the Red Bull teams during the second free practice session.

items.title: Ferrari reveals luxury $4,300 fountain pen inspired by its bespoke supercars
items.summary:
You do not need to buy a Ferrari to spend serious money on the Prancing Horse. Montblanc’s latest collaboration with Maranello has come in the shape of a fountain pen, and it costs more than some used cars.
The Meisterstuck Great Masters Ferrari Tailor Made Inedita Special Edition is for sale for $4,300 in the United States. If you would rather not deal with the messy reloading of such a pen ...Keep reading

items.title: Charles Leclerc reveals Mexican GP overtaking fears after missing out on pole
items.summary:
Charles Leclerc doubts there will be any overtaking in the Mexican Grand Prix, warning the race order will likely be set in the first few corners at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez.
The Ferrari driver topped both of Friday's practice sessions but had to settle for third on the grid. His team-mate and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton claimed his first pole position with the Maranello outfit ...Keep reading

items.summary:

items.title: George Russell identifies costly decision behind Mexican GP qualifying near-miss
items.summary:
George Russell believes an extra lap of fuel cost him pole position for the Mexican Grand Prix after he missed out to his former team-mate and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton by just 0.009 seconds.
The Mercedes driver will start alongside Hamilton on the front row, with Charles Leclerc in third. Russell explained that his rivals had not done preparation laps on their final Q3 runs, while ...Keep reading

items.title: Ocon issues statement after being sidelined by Haas
items.summary: Esteban Ocon has issued a statement acknowledging “a difference in viewpoints” after FP2 was central to his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix, but saying that no physical altercation took place. RACER understands it is highly unlikely Ocon will drive for Haas again this season.
